outcome: Infrastructure funded as an operating expense against actual use, with extra capacity available without a fresh procurement cycle.
overview: Retail infrastructure demand is seasonal and capital planning is annual, which is why estates end up sized for peak and idle for most of the year. APEX moves that infrastructure to a consumption model: capacity is installed on customer premises and paid for against committed and metered use. The decision is financial before it is technical, and it deserves an honest comparison — a committed consumption contract is not the same as elasticity, and the commitment level is what determines whether it is cheaper than buying.

benefits.text: Infrastructure moves from capital purchase to an operating expense against committed use
benefits.limits: Whether this is cheaper depends entirely on the commitment level relative to actual use; an over-committed contract costs more than buying

benefits.text: Capacity above the commitment can be drawn on without a procurement cycle
benefits.limits: Buffer capacity must be installed in advance, so this is faster provisioning rather than cloud-like elasticity

benefits.text: Lifecycle and hardware refresh become the provider’s responsibility rather than a project
benefits.limits: This holds for the length of the contract; if the consumption agreement ends, lifecycle and refresh responsibility reverts to the customer

residency: Equipment is installed on customer premises; data never leaves the customer data centre

notFor.situation: An organisation with stable, predictable demand and available capital
notFor.why: A consumption premium buys flexibility that a stable estate does not use
Capacity must be physically present before it can be consumed, which bounds how quickly it can grow

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with Dell as the consumption provider · Duration: 8–12 weeks from demand profiling to installed capacity under contract
Support model: Provider-held lifecycle, refresh and support under the consumption contract; Redington holds the commercial relationship and the review cadence.
1) Profile — demand measured across a full seasonal cycle, commitment level derived
2) Compare — consumption quotation set against an equivalent capital purchase
3) Install — capacity plus buffer installed and metering established
4) Review and hand over — first quarterly utilisation review completed, cadence handed over
deliverables: The commitment level is traceable to the measured demand profile
A purchase comparison at equivalent capacity is produced and signed by finance
Metered consumption reporting is verifiable against the customer’s own utilisation data
effort: 8–12 weeks from demand profiling to installed capacity under contract
languages: English delivery; Arabic commercial documentation on request
